item.title: Mashiko Pottery Town: Rustic Ceramics & Twice-Yearly Fairs — Guide
item.description: Mashiko-yaki, the pottery of Mashiko, has been produced since the 1850s and gained international recognition through the mingei (folk craft) movement led by potter Shoji Hamada in the 20th century, prized for its rustic, earthy glazes and unpretentious functional beauty. The town is home to several hundred kilns and studios, many open for browsing and hands-on workshops, and twice each year — during the Mashiko Pottery Fair each May and November, alongside a related autumn Ceramic Art Week — hundreds of additional vendors set up stalls, transforming the town into one of Japan’s largest pottery markets.
